Sasria Buckles as KZN Business hangs in the balance

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Thousands of KZN businesses are waiting for their riot insurance payouts but many cannot afford to wait much longer

Unique Selling Point:
Very strong case studies with visual material of what happened to their businesses and a broker who has a big picture vision of the business devastation

Summary:
SASRIA is a state owned enterprise that falls under national treasury. For years businesses have been paying mandatory premiums to cover them in the wake of political riots and violence. After the insurrection SASRIA received about 10 000 claims and the financial loss has been touted as being in excess of R20 billion rand. As at March 2020 Sasria had total assets of R8.9 billion. SASRIA has issues a press release saying they have engaged with National Treasury and the Prudential authority about possible solutions should the worst case scenario in terms of damages materialise

Further information:
Brett Chapman who is a part owner of Fashion X, a clothing manufacturer has submitted a claim for about R12 million. His business had just begun to turn a corner after Edcon went into business rescue. Now they are on the ropes again. Last week the IDC came to their rescue but they are still waiting for SASRIA to pay out - had the IDC not stepped in- Fashion X would have gone under. All his stock was being made at factories in Newcastle. 11 Clothing factories were looted and burned and he lost all those orders.
Pete Jansen Van Vuuren had a hardware and building supply shop in the Valley of a thousand hills. Everything was looted. Even the retaining walls were removed, the electrical cables out of the ground and the lintels above the door. He cannot lock his shop because there is nothing to lock. He has a claim of R1.7 million rand and if it isnt paid out soon, he will close the shop and find another profession. He is heartbroken. He had staff living on the premises and he says they literally ran for their lives. He can hold out for another month, not more. He says he has to laugh because otherwise he cries. They even removed the cobbled paving.
Cheryl Searle has a packaging company that packs for amongst others Nivea South Africa. They watched remotely as their factory was invaded. It wasnt burnt thanks to what they call the Riot Squad- taxi bosses who have now become their security company. They arrived with 15 armed guards and stayed for 3 days. They have a claim for about R2million because they have managed to get up and rolling on their own steam and get back vehicles with the help of the taxi bosses. She has never seen the army in that area and says there are no ATM's and very few businesses up and running. Aubrey surname? will get is a part owner in the Spar in Umlazi - it was the first SPAR in a township the area where the SPAR was has been burnt down and its like a ghost town. They too are still waiting. ( More information coming) Carte Blanche puts tough questions to SASRIA and looks at the implications to the KZN economy if these businesses arent compensated soon

FINAL SCRIPT SASRIA BUCKLES TX SUNDAY 10th OCTOBER 2021

Commentary One
On the 10th July this year Aubrey Kubheka, a co-owner of the Umlazi Megacity and Philani Valley Mall Spar’s, heard a rumour there may be unrest, and decided to close his stores early.

Then Jacob Zuma’s supporters unleashed hell across KZN and Gauteng

Kubheka watched as 17 years of work was demolished overnight

Aubrey
We couldn’t defend ourselves, we found ourselves in a situation where we were helpless and we had to just sit back and watch

Commentary two
Of his 17 businesses, 12 were looted and vandalized and some burnt

Aubrey
Most of my stores and managers phoned the police, one store phoned the police over 100 times and nothing was done, even this store we didn’t get help.
Derek
What was it like when you got to your stores?
Aubrey
It was bad, it was really bad, stuff still burning, stock on the floor. I would say 30% of the stock was just tramped on, and I must say some of my staff were on those sites and trying to guard the little that they could save

Link
At this massive store in Umlazi it wasn’t just the entire stock that was looted, the tills were destroyed, the offices and equipment burnt and even the copper wiring and tubes were stripped from the ceiling.

Aubrey Kubheka
We have a lot to fix here. We are looking at the tune of R24 million to get the store up and running again
Derek
That is just one store?
Aubrey
it’s shocking what we are faced with.

Commentary three
As anarchy and death spread across KZN and Gauteng, and businesses tried to fend for themselves, Duduzane Zuma recorded a video message

Up sound Duduzane Zuma
For the people that are protesting and looting, please do so carefully and responsibly
Commentary Four
But no one was listening, and when the flames were finally doused, more than 300 people were dead, damage north of R20 billion Rands recorded, and thousands of jobs had been lost- some forever.

Derek
What is the total effect on your staff at these stores
Aubrey
Over 500 people are sitting at home. We have been frantically trying to apply for them through the unrest fund that the president has made available, but we are facing a lot of challenges, the system crashes and in the last two months none of the staff have been paid
Derek
So how are they getting by?
Aubrey
Derek, I don’t know.t really really breaks my heart

Commentary five
Khubeka is desperate to begin rebuilding, but until his insurance pays out he must wait. Because a bottleneck lies with SASRIA

Derek Link
You may not have heard of SASRIA, possibly because it’s one of the better run State owned Enterprises, it provides the massive financial back up to private insurance companies when it comes to cover for riots and acts of terrorism

Commentary six
SASRIA is the only game in town for this kind of cover, so as more than 9000 claims poured into their offices they struggled to cope.

Stuart Pringle is a Durban based broker who says time is critical right now

Derek
So can you explain this bottleneck?
Stuart
Basically, it's as simple as a capacity issue. There's at least 8000 claims. So you can just do the simple mathematics. If you've if you've got 10 claims handlers, that's 800 claims per claims handler
Derek
all waiting in the queue
Stuart
All waiting in the queue.

Commentary seven
Pringle believes the delays are a national emergency and SASRIA should reach out for help from the insurance industry


Stuart PRINGLE
It’s not only affecting the first tier of business, it's affecting the second tier as well, without payments coming through and without people being able to rebuild their businesses. We are staring down the barrel.

Commentary eight
Small business owner Peter Jansen Van Vuuren owns a hardware store and small factory just above the Valley of a thousand hills.

Peter
I had a phone call from a staff member of mine telling me that he was going to die. He lived on the property and he just said he doesn't know what to do he said there was probably about 100, 150 people on the property, and afterwards the line went dead and when I phoned him later, he said he was able to jump over the wall and hide in the bush.

Commentary nine
Some of his staff lived on the property

Peter
They had the clothes on their back, they picked up their children and they ran for their lives.

Peter opens factory door

Commentary ten
By the time he was able to get back to the shop safely, Peter was greeted by ruins

Peter
After the initial stuff that disappeared, it probably took them another four to five days to finish clearing out. By that stage, they were really starting to remove roofing, taking out door frames, taking out window frames, taking out lintels and everything else. And then they stripped the rest of the building -the power, the cables- they've even taken, the UG fittings out of the septic tanks.
Derek
right down to the lintels on the doors?
Peter
And the retaining walls, the blocks out of the walls gone. They even gone so far now as to taking out the municipal cable coming in from the road, so where your electrical meter is – that is even gone

Derek
Peter, the first time you looked at your business that you'd developed over the years, is it possible to describe?
Peter begins to weep..
Derek
Hey, Peter...I can see it's not just your business, though, is it? I mean, it's your family and it's your staff?
Peter
And they sitting now hey, what do we do? Twenty five staff. It’s not only them, it’s their families their children, the effects on small businesses is going to be felt for many many years to come

Commentary eleven
At the Philani Valley Mall where Aubrey Kubheka has a Spar and a Tops, he took us on a walkabout. Here small businesses have been shattered

Music montage

The sound of customers and trade, replaced with the wind and banging bits of detritus that echo out of the broken shops. A dentist, A doctor, a dialysis centre, a funeral parlour, and other hopes and dreams, all dashed. Even the post office has been hollowed out- possibly never to return

Aubrey
I am getting calls every day from the community members in Philane, they want us to come and open the store – they have volunteered to clean the store and guard the Centre so that we can be able to trade

Commentary twelve
But he doesn’t know if this Spar will ever open again, the damage done here was so extensive.

Derek
You used to have all the camera’s here?
Aubrey
All the screens of camera’s here
Derek
What’s next door? This was the cash office
Aubrey
This was the cash office
Derek
They just destroyed a couple of safes here
Aubrey
They must have used heavy duty equipment to get in here. It breaks my heart. I don’t even want to come here anymore

LINK
For these shops to reopen there has to be a long chain reaction but so many of the links are broken and it starts with the landlords who haven’t even started to repair the shopping centres because they haven’t got the money

Commentary Thirteen
They are all waiting for SASRIA.


Derek
You made out the claim and then you waited?
Aubrey
And then we waited
Derek
And waited

Commentary fourteen
And then just days before we met Kubheka, SASRIA paid out 75% of his stock claim.
SASRIA isn’t doing interviews, but in a written response it said:

We have started paying interim payments... on all big claims (above R30 million) and we are determined to make sure that at least 30% of total claim value is paid in the next couple of weeks

Derek
Give us an idea of the size of these claims?
Derek these claims are huge, huge, huge. Our stock claim alone was about R80 million. Our equipment claim was about R70 million
Derek
Now that 75% of the stock you have been paid out for, that was stock that was sitting in here that you haven’t paid your suppliers for?
Aubrey
Yes that was the stock that was looted.
Derek
So in other words that doesn’t come into your pocket?
Aubrey
No, no, no, it’s not mine, it’s for all the small suppliers, the fruit and veg guy. It’s not my money and it’s still not 100% we still short 25%

Commentary fifteen
Clint Du Toit is amongst others, a chemical supplier to the electroplating industry. He too is waiting for Sasria’s pay out. His factory is on a main arterial about a kilometre up the hill from Watercrest Mall, where this happened

Up sound Watercrest Mall
Absolute chaos. Unbelievable, Watercrest Mall is absolutely destroyed

Commentary sixteen
From the mall the looters made their way past the factory, then broke in to steal the forklift, to continue looting.

Up sound of Derek and Clint
So the forklift obviously came through here, reversed with his forks up, and took this whole roof off, and it fell on top of him and then he recovered, and went down the road to be used as a transport.


Commentary seventeen
The office block was burnt to a cinder, destroying years of records and formulations, but Du Toit considers himself lucky, because the factory was saved

Derek
we've been looking at the carnage around KZN, and a small miracle here?
Clint Du Toit
Yes, we were very lucky that the geyser burst and we actually isolated the fire just to the office admin block
Derek
Looking at what if, if the fire came through- we are surrounded by chemicals, what would have happened?
Clint
A lot of the methanol’s and stuff we have on site would have exploded. A lot of people in the streets, all the looters would have been hurt, so it’s not a what if I want to even think about, it would have been catastrophic

Commentary eighteen
The lab is the heart of their business and a looter knocked over a hazardous solvent which filled the room so they hurried away, stealing only computers

Derek
Amazing, really, that the geyser burst to save the fire spreading here to the factory, and the solvent was spilt in the laboratory, saving multi-million rand equipment and the bonsai tree survived.
Clint
Yes, the bonsai’s survived

Commentary nineteen
Miraculously so have the jobs. Amos Gumede began as Du Toit’s gardener. Today he runs the factory and oversees safety – trained and encouraged by his boss.

Derek
You must be very proud of what you have achieved?
Yes I worked hard for it
Derek
Amos on that dreadful night how did you get the news?
Amos
Even me I cried when my boss told me the factory was burning because I know where we come from until we here, and if those things disappear so easily I feel bad. Today I am working and I thank God, because across the road about 400 people lost their jobs

Commentary twenty
While they wait for the payout, Clint Du Toit’s office staff are all crammed into the factory boardroom

Clint
That's what you have to do and we have to keep going. You stay in the game

Derek
How is it changing how you think about your business in the future?
Clint
I’ve had other opportunities now in different provinces. I think this area is a very, very volatile area. I will not invest any more into this except for fixing it up and getting it to a workable thing. We are looking at building two factories, one in PE and one in Cape Town. I think that is a bit more of a stable area.

Up Sound Vision Packaging factory

Commentary twenty one
If there is light at the end of the tunnel, it can be found here at Cheryl Searle’s family owned packaging business that employs 70 staff.

Up sound in factory

But as the looters burned the nearby storage units and people broke into their factory on the 12th July, there was no light at all.

Cheryl
I felt absolutely helpless. We tried everyone, called the police, the local security, 1011. Nobody answered. Nobody did anything. And then I got hold of some people around the area and I said, someone's got to help us. This is just crazy.

Commentary twenty- two
Help came and they managed to get the looters out and save the factory. Then later the community security came to their rescue and helped recover their truck and forklift. This co-operation has created new bonds between them and the local people

Cheryl
And then they were the ones who said, No, we know where your truck's going to be. We know where your forklift is. They know the people, they know what's happening. And they were absolutely amazing.

Commentary Twenty- three
With the recoveries and by doing some repairs themselves, they have reduced their claim substantially from R8 million. SASRIA have made an interim payment, but the company is still waiting for the balance to pay lost wages

Derek
Cheryl, you've got a close relationship with your staff. What are they saying about those days of strife and mayhem?
Cheryl
Well, they couldn't believe it, and I showed them a video of truck vehicles loading from the value logistics, and they were absolutely horrified when they recognized one of the vehicles to be the taxi they catch to come to work every day. And they said how gunjane na...speaks zulu

DEREK
Which means? ( REDO IN VOICE OVER)
Cheryl
Here's our car! This is the one that brings us to work here. He's loading goods from Value. And they just shook their heads and they keep saying to me, we just we just thank you for having our jobs still

Commentary Twenty four
Sasria has assured Carte Blanche that everyone will get paid, and the day after our interview
SASRIA paid out Jansen Van Vuuren claim. It plans to settle all claims below a million by end September 2021, and they are determined to settle 80% of all claims between R1 million and R30 million by the end of this October.

Derek
So out of this disaster, there are a few shimmers of light.
Cheryl There's definitely lots of shimmers of light. We, for some unknown reason have been blessed with more business.
Derek
But the Sasria payment would be useful?
Cheryl
Well, that would be a bonus, wouldn't it, because that would just take us to the next level.

THE END 15 00

PROMO ONE 11 seconds
Almost three months after the July riots ripped apart KZN businesses, they’re still reeling. Is the state owned insurance company SASRIA paying claims fast enough?

PROMO TWO 15 seconds
The July unrest was catastrophic for business in KZN. Now desperate to start rebuilding, they are waiting for SASRIA – the state owned insurance company that is the only cover they have against riots and terrorism

Derek
You made out the claims and then you waited?
Aubrey
And then we waited
Derek
And waited

PROMO THREE
Business owners across KZN have counted the costs, submitted their claims and now they want to rebuild
Aubrey
This was the cash office
Derek
They just destroyed a couple of safes here
Aubrey
They must have used heavy duty equipment to get in here. It breaks my heart.

Stuart Pringle is a Durban based broker who says time is critical right now Derek So can you explain this bottleneck? Stuart Basically, it's as simple as a capacity issue. There's at least 8000 claims. So you can just do the simple mathematics. If you've if you've got 10 claims handlers, that's 800 claims per claims handler Derek all waiting in the queue Stuart All waiting in the queue. Commentary seven Pringle believes the delays are a national emergency and SASRIA should reach out for help from the insurance industry Stuart PRINGLE It’s not only affecting the first tier of business, it's affecting the second tier as well, without payments coming through and without people being able to rebuild their businesses. We are staring down the barrel. Commentary eight Small business owner Peter Jansen Van Vuuren owns a hardware store and small factory just above the Valley of a thousand hills. Peter I had a phone call from a staff member of mine telling me that he was going to die. He lived on the property and he just said he doesn't know what to do he said there was probably about 100, 150 people on the property, and afterwards the line went dead and when I phoned him later, he said he was able to jump over the wall and hide in the bush. Commentary nine Some of his staff lived on the property Peter They had the clothes on their back, they picked up their children and they ran for their lives. Peter opens factory door Commentary ten By the time he was able to get back to the shop safely, Peter was greeted by ruins Peter After the initial stuff that disappeared, it probably took them another four to five days to finish clearing out. By that stage, they were really starting to remove roofing, taking out door frames, taking out window frames, taking out lintels and everything else. And then they stripped the rest of the building -the power, the cables- they've even taken, the UG fittings out of the septic tanks. Derek right down to the lintels on the doors? Peter And the retaining walls, the blocks out of the walls gone. They even gone so far now as to taking out the municipal cable coming in from the road, so where your electrical meter is – that is even gone Derek Peter, the first time you looked at your business that you'd developed over the years, is it possible to describe? Peter begins to weep.. Derek Hey, Peter...I can see it's not just your business, though, is it? I mean, it's your family and it's your staff? Peter And they sitting now hey, what do we do? Twenty five staff. It’s not only them, it’s their families their children, the effects on small businesses is going to be felt for many many years to come Commentary eleven At the Philani Valley Mall where Aubrey Kubheka has a Spar and a Tops, he took us on a walkabout. Here small businesses have been shattered Music montage The sound of customers and trade, replaced with the wind and banging bits of detritus that echo out of the broken shops. A dentist, A doctor, a dialysis centre, a funeral parlour, and other hopes and dreams, all dashed. Even the post office has been hollowed out- possibly never to return Aubrey I am getting calls every day from the community members in Philane, they want us to come and open the store – they have volunteered to clean the store and guard the Centre so that we can be able to trade Commentary twelve But he doesn’t know if this Spar will ever open again, the damage done here was so extensive. Derek You used to have all the camera’s here? Aubrey All the screens of camera’s here Derek What’s next door? This was the cash office Aubrey This was the cash office Derek They just destroyed a couple of safes here Aubrey They must have used heavy duty equipment to get in here. It breaks my heart. I don’t even want to come here anymore LINK For these shops to reopen there has to be a long chain reaction but so many of the links are broken and it starts with the landlords who haven’t even started to repair the shopping centres because they haven’t got the money Commentary Thirteen They are all waiting for SASRIA. Derek You made out the claim and then you waited? Aubrey And then we waited Derek And waited Commentary fourteen And then just days before we met Kubheka, SASRIA paid out 75% of his stock claim. SASRIA isn’t doing interviews, but in a written response it said: We have started paying interim payments... on all big claims (above R30 million) and we are determined to make sure that at least 30% of total claim value is paid in the next couple of weeks Derek Give us an idea of the size of these claims? Derek these claims are huge, huge, huge. Our stock claim alone was about R80 million. Our equipment claim was about R70 million Derek Now that 75% of the stock you have been paid out for, that was stock that was sitting in here that you haven’t paid your suppliers for? Aubrey Yes that was the stock that was looted. Derek So in other words that doesn’t come into your pocket? Aubrey No, no, no, it’s not mine, it’s for all the small suppliers, the fruit and veg guy. It’s not my money and it’s still not 100% we still short 25% Commentary fifteen Clint Du Toit is amongst others, a chemical supplier to the electroplating industry. He too is waiting for Sasria’s pay out. His factory is on a main arterial about a kilometre up the hill from Watercrest Mall, where this happened Up sound Watercrest Mall Absolute chaos. Unbelievable, Watercrest Mall is absolutely destroyed Commentary sixteen From the mall the looters made their way past the factory, then broke in to steal the forklift, to continue looting. Up sound of Derek and Clint So the forklift obviously came through here, reversed with his forks up, and took this whole roof off, and it fell on top of him and then he recovered, and went down the road to be used as a transport. Commentary seventeen The office block was burnt to a cinder, destroying years of records and formulations, but Du Toit considers himself lucky, because the factory was saved Derek we've been looking at the carnage around KZN, and a small miracle here? Clint Du Toit Yes, we were very lucky that the geyser burst and we actually isolated the fire just to the office admin block Derek Looking at what if, if the fire came through- we are surrounded by chemicals, what would have happened? Clint A lot of the methanol’s and stuff we have on site would have exploded. A lot of people in the streets, all the looters would have been hurt, so it’s not a what if I want to even think about, it would have been catastrophic Commentary eighteen The lab is the heart of their business and a looter knocked over a hazardous solvent which filled the room so they hurried away, stealing only computers Derek Amazing, really, that the geyser burst to save the fire spreading here to the factory, and the solvent was spilt in the laboratory, saving multi-million rand equipment and the bonsai tree survived. Clint Yes, the bonsai’s survived Commentary nineteen Miraculously so have the jobs. Amos Gumede began as Du Toit’s gardener. Today he runs the factory and oversees safety – trained and encouraged by his boss. Derek You must be very proud of what you have achieved? Yes I worked hard for it Derek Amos on that dreadful night how did you get the news? Amos Even me I cried when my boss told me the factory was burning because I know where we come from until we here, and if those things disappear so easily I feel bad. Today I am working and I thank God, because across the road about 400 people lost their jobs Commentary twenty While they wait for the payout, Clint Du Toit’s office staff are all crammed into the factory boardroom Clint That's what you have to do and we have to keep going. You stay in the game Derek How is it changing how you think about your business in the future? Clint I’ve had other opportunities now in different provinces. I think this area is a very, very volatile area. I will not invest any more into this except for fixing it up and getting it to a workable thing. We are looking at building two factories, one in PE and one in Cape Town. I think that is a bit more of a stable area. Up Sound Vision Packaging factory Commentary twenty one If there is light at the end of the tunnel, it can be found here at Cheryl Searle’s family owned packaging business that employs 70 staff. Up sound in factory But as the looters burned the nearby storage units and people broke into their factory on the 12th July, there was no light at all. Cheryl I felt absolutely helpless. We tried everyone, called the police, the local security, 1011. Nobody answered. Nobody did anything. And then I got hold of some people around the area and I said, someone's got to help us. This is just crazy. Commentary twenty- two Help came and they managed to get the looters out and save the factory. Then later the community security came to their rescue and helped recover their truck and forklift. This co-operation has created new bonds between them and the local people Cheryl And then they were the ones who said, No, we know where your truck's going to be. We know where your forklift is. They know the people, they know what's happening. And they were absolutely amazing. Commentary Twenty- three With the recoveries and by doing some repairs themselves, they have reduced their claim substantially from R8 million. SASRIA have made an interim payment, but the company is still waiting for the balance to pay lost wages Derek Cheryl, you've got a close relationship with your staff. What are they saying about those days of strife and mayhem? Cheryl Well, they couldn't believe it, and I showed them a video of truck vehicles loading from the value logistics, and they were absolutely horrified when they recognized one of the vehicles to be the taxi they catch to come to work every day. And they said how gunjane na...speaks zulu DEREK Which means? ( REDO IN VOICE OVER) Cheryl Here's our car! This is the one that brings us to work here. He's loading goods from Value. And they just shook their heads and they keep saying to me, we just we just thank you for having our jobs still Commentary Twenty four Sasria has assured Carte Blanche that everyone will get paid, and the day after our interview SASRIA paid out Jansen Van Vuuren claim. It plans to settle all claims below a million by end September 2021, and they are determined to settle 80% of all claims between R1 million and R30 million by the end of this October. Derek So out of this disaster, there are a few shimmers of light. Cheryl There's definitely lots of shimmers of light. We, for some unknown reason have been blessed with more business. Derek But the Sasria payment would be useful? Cheryl Well, that would be a bonus, wouldn't it, because that would just take us to the next level. THE END 15 00 PROMO ONE 11 seconds Almost three months after the July riots ripped apart KZN businesses, they’re still reeling. Is the state owned insurance company SASRIA paying claims fast enough? PROMO TWO 15 seconds The July unrest was catastrophic for business in KZN. Now desperate to start rebuilding, they are waiting for SASRIA – the state owned insurance company that is the only cover they have against riots and terrorism Derek You made out the claims and then you waited? Aubrey And then we waited Derek And waited PROMO THREE Business owners across KZN have counted the costs, submitted their claims and now they want to rebuild Aubrey This was the cash office Derek They just destroyed a couple of safes here Aubrey They must have used heavy duty equipment to get in here. It breaks my heart. Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Sasria Buckles as KZN Business hangs in the balance (6003 ) Joy Summers 06 October 2021

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Thousands of KZN businesses are waiting for their riot insurance payouts but many cannot afford to wait much longer
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Very strong case studies with visual material of what happened to their businesses and a broker who has a big picture vision of the business devastation
metadata.Summary: SASRIA is a state owned enterprise that falls under national treasury. For years businesses have been paying mandatory premiums to cover them in the wake of political riots and violence. After the insurrection SASRIA received about 10 000 claims and the financial loss has been touted as being in excess of R20 billion rand. As at March 2020 Sasria had total assets of R8.9 billion. SASRIA has issues a press release saying they have engaged with National Treasury and the Prudential authority about possible solutions should the worst case scenario in terms of damages materialise
metadata.Further information: Brett Chapman who is a part owner of Fashion X, a clothing manufacturer has submitted a claim for about R12 million. His business had just begun to turn a corner after Edcon went into business rescue. Now they are on the ropes again. Last week the IDC came to their rescue but they are still waiting for SASRIA to pay out - had the IDC not stepped in- Fashion X would have gone under. All his stock was being made at factories in Newcastle. 11 Clothing factories were looted and burned and he lost all those orders. Pete Jansen Van Vuuren had a hardware and building supply shop in the Valley of a thousand hills. Everything was looted. Even the retaining walls were removed, the electrical cables out of the ground and the lintels above the door. He cannot lock his shop because there is nothing to lock. He has a claim of R1.7 million rand and if it isnt paid out soon, he will close the shop and find another profession. He is heartbroken. He had staff living on the premises and he says they literally ran for their lives. He can hold out for another month, not more. He says he has to laugh because otherwise he cries. They even removed the cobbled paving. Cheryl Searle has a packaging company that packs for amongst others Nivea South Africa. They watched remotely as their factory was invaded. It wasnt burnt thanks to what they call the Riot Squad- taxi bosses who have now become their security company. They arrived with 15 armed guards and stayed for 3 days. They have a claim for about R2million because they have managed to get up and rolling on their own steam and get back vehicles with the help of the taxi bosses. She has never seen the army in that area and says there are no ATM's and very few businesses up and running. Aubrey surname? will get is a part owner in the Spar in Umlazi - it was the first SPAR in a township the area where the SPAR was has been burnt down and its like a ghost town. They too are still waiting. ( More information coming) Carte Blanche puts tough questions to SASRIA and looks at the implications to the KZN economy if these businesses arent compensated soon
